key_insight: Surrogate-guided reinforcement learning enriched virtual perovskite recipe shortlists near high-performing measured devices, without demonstrating experimental performance gains.
engineering_relevance: The framework could help prioritize perovskite solar-cell recipes before costly fabrication and testing.
method: Generate candidate recipes with reinforcement-learning policies guided by a frozen TabPFN surrogate.
Assess neighborhood support using a reference pool of 890 measured devices.
Compare three learned policies with six baselines using 3,000 surrogate evaluations per run.
evidence_signal: Five-fold evaluation on 1,846 devices raised mean PCE from 19.68% to 23.74% through top-ten selection; top-100 neighborhood-supported hit rates reached 23–24% for PPO/RPPO versus 2.9% for Pure Random and 10% for the strongest baselines.
watch_item: Many generated recipes had weak experimental-neighborhood support, and experimental performance, seed robustness, and matched-budget advantage remain unestablished.
paper_title: Enrichment-Oriented Virtual Screening of Perovskite Solar Cells through Reinforcement Learning
